- When sentiment is consistently neutral or negative, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 3–8% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.5 for 3+ consecutive days), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often underestimates mean reversion; add 1–3% to forecast if recent 18-day average is below 30-day average.
- When sentiment is negative and price is falling, model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted upward by 1–3% to account for sentiment-driven reversal.
- If sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +0.5 and -0.5), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use 3-day moving average to smooth and adjust forecast.
